title: Rollout ceremony and playback protocol (WIP)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc sketches a lightweight "playback" ceremony and checklist for cross-functional LLM feature rollouts. The goal is to provide a repeatable rehearsal (playback) that exercises: routing rules, model fallbacks, cost-safeguard triggers, observability signal alignment, and communication handoffs across Product, Serving, SRE, and Support.

Key principles (why this is different):
- Treat rollout as a choreography, not a one-team event. The "playback" is a short, observable rehearsal that reproduces a restricted end-to-end exposure and then replays failure scenarios.
- Prefer measurable signals and single-source-of-truth dashboards (Console route + SLO cards) for go/no-go decisions.
- Keep scope small: table-stakes are routing, KV-cache behavior, latency, unit cost, and response quality.

When to run a playback
- Pre-canary: run at least once for any feature that changes routing, model variants, or response shaping.
- Pre-global: run immediately before any >10% traffic expansion.
- Post-incident: run as part of a remediation checklist if a rollout contributed to an outage.

Participants and roles (30–60m rehearsal):
- Owner (Product/PM) — leads ceremony, reads the hypothesis and acceptance criteria.
- Runbook Lead (Ops/SE) — triggers traffic slices, initiates failovers, runs test traffic.
- Serving Engineer — observes model runtime metrics and kernel/quantization toggles.
- SRE — watches infra alarms, scaling behavior, and circuit-breaker state.
- Data/Quality rep — evaluates quality signals and sample responses.
- Support buddy — prepares canned messages and incident channel.

Pre-playback checklist (async prep, must be green before the meeting):
- Owner has published the hypothesis and the rollback decision tree in the ticket. (Jira INF-3864 or equivalent)
- Canary route and experiment flags config reviewed in Console: route id, model variant ids, cohort allocation, TTL for caching.
- Test harness: a seeded corpus (100–500 prompts) representing the top N user flows (stored in Confluence Playback Lab Notes).
- Observability: per-route SLOs wired to the experiment (p50/p95 latency, error rate, per-token cost). Dashboards pre-built and pinned.
- Safety knobs: cost-rate-limit, per-route token cap, automatic fallback variant and region routing configured.

Playback ceremony agenda (recommended 45 minutes)
1) 5m — Read hypothesis + acceptance criteria (owner). Example acceptance criteria:
   - No more than +7% p95 latency vs baseline (10k-sample),
   - Error rate increase <0.2 ppts in first 24h,
   - Quality regression (automated eval) <= 2% on golden prompts,
   - Unit cost delta <= +12% or manual approval required.
2) 10m — Synthetic canary: run seeded corpus against the canary route at scaled throughput (x1.5 normal) to observe steady-state and cache warmup.
   - Check: model selection logs, KV-cache hit rate, batch sizes, GPU utilization.
3) 10m — Failure rehearsals (one at a time):
   - a) Simulate model OOM / high latency: mark variant unhealthy and let routing fall back to safe variant. Observe latency and fallthrough.
   - b) Simulate region outage: route traffic to alternate region/pool and confirm data-plane connectivity.
   - c) Simulate cost runaway: trigger synthetic high-token requests and validate per-route token throttle triggers.
4) 10m — A/B split sanity: re-run subset of corpus with A/B traffic split and compare automated evals + user-visible samples.
5) 10m — Communication and rollback drill: run the incident channel playbook, post the prepared support message, and validate rollback steps (route switch, feature flag, and automatic fallback) finish within target time (target <6m for full rollback).

Playbook snippets (commands / Console actions)
- Create temporary traffic slice: Console -> Routes -> Duplicate route -> set cohort to 2% and name it "playback-temp".
- Attach model variant: set variant pin to v2-quant-8bit; confirm contract with tokenization test.
- Failover test: mark variant unhealthy via API: POST /api/internal/variants/{id}/mark-unhealthy -> observe route log stream.
- Trigger cost throttle: POST /api/internal/test/token-storm?route=playback-temp&tokens=100000

Signals to watch (single-line definitions):
- p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, infra_error_rate_pct, model_error_rate_pct, kv_cache_hit_pct, avg_batch_size, tokens_per_request, per_token_usd, eval_regression_pct.

Decision matrix (quick):
- Green: all acceptance criteria met -> proceed to live canary.
- Amber: only cost or latency slightly over threshold -> hold, discuss mitigations (lower cohort, enable heavier quantization, increase batch target).
- Red: quality regression > threshold or error rate spike -> immediate rollback; create incident ticket and follow RCA pipeline.

Fallback lanes (priority):
1) Soft fallback: route to pinned older variant in same region.
2) Regional fallback: route to dedicated pool in alternate region.
3) Degraded mode: enable condensed-response template (shorter max tokens) to protect latency/cost.
4) Full revert: switch feature flag off and redirect to baseline route.

Post-playback artifacts (deliverables within 24h):
- Playback log export: timestamped route logs + sample responses (Owner).
- Signal diff report: baseline vs playback for all tracked metrics (Ops).
- Quality audit: top 20 failed golden prompts with manual notes (Data/Quality).
- Follow-ups: list of action items with owners and SLAs (1d, 3d, 2w).

Common gotchas and tips:
- Cache/TTL mismatch: rehearsals often mislead because production caches are hotter; explicitly simulate cold-cache runs.
- Quantization slip: binary-compatible artifacts can change tokenization heuristics; always include tokenization smoke tests.
- Hidden dependencies: third-party tools (search, vector store) can be the real source of latency; include them in the seeded corpus where possible.
- Over-automation risk: automation that flips routes without human-in-the-loop can escalate unexpected quality regressions; ensure the first <5% expansion is manual.

Example quick template (copyable for Jira ticket):
Hypothesis: "V2 response generator reduces hallucination on product descriptions by >=6% while not increasing p95 latency >7% and cost < +12%."
Acceptance criteria: [list from above]
Playback test date: YYYY-MM-DD
Participants: [names]
Seed corpus link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Playback+Lab+Notes
Canary route id: route-prod-ads-v2-playback-temp
Rollback steps: 1) pin route to variant v1-stable 2) lower cohort to 0% 3) toggle feature flag off

Next steps (owner action items):
- Aisha: schedule playback and attach seeded corpus (by EOD).
- Theo: prepare the variant health API endpoint and sample logs (48h).
- Marina: prebuild the per-route SLO dashboard and share link (24h).
- Jordan: draft the support canned messages and incident channel template (24h).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep ceremony <60m or teams won't show up.
- Capture at least 500 synthetic requests during the synthetic canary to stabilize p95 numbers.
- For private/Dedicated customers, add one extra rehearsal for networking and KMS checks.

Open questions (to resolve before first production run):
- Should the cost throttle be a hard quota or a soft alert for hosted vs dedicated customers? (ops/product)
- Who has permission to execute full revert for private deployments — SRE or customer success?

End of draft.
